name: Autocracy
summary: Autocracy is a form of government in which one person, or a small group, holds total power that no law, assembly or electorate limits. Tullock groups dictatorships and hereditary kingdoms and empires under the word, and sets it apart from governments that proceed by voting and from feudal ones. The defining sources say who holds power and how it is held, and say nothing on economics, society or foreign policy.
scope: The general form of government the name stands for: rule by one person (autocrat, dictator, hereditary king or emperor) or a small group with unlimited power, as defined by two dictionaries and by Tullock's study Autocracy. It is audited as a family; answers come only from those definitions. Russian tsarist autocracy, absolutism and totalitarianism are separate entries and their texts are not used.

sources.usedFor: Definition: a form of government in which a country is ruled by a person or group with total power.

sources.title: Autocracy
sources.author: Gordon Tullock
sources.usedFor: Scope of the term (dictatorships, kingdoms and empires; not electoral or feudal governments) and the contrast with electoral systems.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Autocracy is defined as government by a person or group with unlimited or total power, so no law made by the ruler or predecessors binds him.

strong-leader.rationale: Autocracy is rule by one person with unlimited power, so the leader is by definition free of legislatures and gridlock; the sources define this but do not argue the benefit.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Where all power sits in one ruler, he commands the armed forces and picks the government with no legislature to share it, as the definitions of unlimited authority and Tullock's dictators and kings describe.

separated-powers.rationale: Power held wholly by one person or small group is the opposite of power divided among bodies that check each other.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Tullock excludes governments that proceed by voting of a considerable number of people from autocracy, and unlimited personal power leaves no supreme parliament.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: An autocrat with total power needs no assembly's approval to spend; Tullock separates autocracy from governments that depend on voting.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: A rights document that ordinary majorities cannot amend would limit a government whose power is defined as unlimited.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The statement presumes a ruler bound by constitutional laws, which contradicts a ruler defined as holding unlimited authority.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule only through announced standing laws would bind a ruler whose power is defined as unlimited, so autocracy rejects it.

democracy-best.rationale: Tullock treats governments that depend on voting as not autocratic, and the dictionaries define autocracy as rule by one person or a small group, so calling democracy best contradicts it.
